note: Hijacking (src/systems/vehicles/hijack.gd). On foot or on your own speeder, within reach of a ship or speeder someone else sits in, E hops you up onto it (hop_s seconds, an arc hop_arc_m above the line), then the one at the controls is thrown out and you take them. ship_reach_m / speeder_reach_m: how far from the vehicle's middle across the ground you may be; ship_rise_m / speeder_rise_m: how far above or below it (a jetpack gets you up to a ship hovering low). ship_top_m / speeder_top_m: where on the vehicle you land, above its middle. The thrown-out pilot lands on their feet on the ground beside it, victim_damage hurt, pushed away at victim_push m/s (fading by victim_push_fade). Over LAN the vehicle's own game decides: the hijacker waits at most wait_s on top for its answer, then drops off. The ship or speeder you take is theirs: when you get out (or eject) it is back in their game where you left it, on the ground below; crash it and it is wrecked in theirs too (their primary waits for T-89's patch-up). An AI pilot (the Remnant interceptor, while it flies low enough to reach) is thrown clear and the ship is stolen, as one taken off its pad. cooldown_s: after a hop ends, how long before another.
